title: Associate Professor of Oral Medicine, Infection, and Immunity
bio: Dr. David M. Kim received his DDS from the University of Maryland Dental School and completed his periodontology training and Doctor of Medical Science (DMSc) in oral biology at the Harvard School of Dental Medicine (HSDM). He is an associate professor at HSDM. Kim is a past recipient of the Joseph L. Henry Award for excellence in research and clinical training from Harvard. He has also received the Balint Orban Research Award, the Award for Outstanding Teaching and Mentoring in Periodontics, and a Teaching Fellowship from the American Academy of Periodontology. Additionally, he has been honored with both Junior and Senior Faculty Awards from HSDM. Kim’s clinical and research interests focus on using innovative concepts, technologies, and biomaterials to enhance intraoral soft and hard tissue formation. His work emphasizes incorporating tissue engineering to repair and regenerate soft and hard tissue volume for patients requiring dental implants. His interest in bone regeneration and dental implant therapies has led to extensive publication in peer-reviewed journals and textbooks. Kim is a diplomate of the American Board of Periodontology.
